learningObjective: Explain how TorchInductor handles an op that has no direct lowering (falls back to the ATen implementation) and what that means for kernel structure.

canonicalClaims.claim: When TorchInductor encounters an op with no lowering but with an ATen implementation, it inserts an ATen fallback call in the generated wrapper at that position; surrounding ops still compile to Triton, and the opaque op forms a fusion boundary.
conditions: The op has a valid ATen implementation and meta impl.
nonImplications: Does not imply that ATen fallbacks are always slow.
Does not imply fallbacks are unavoidable; a user-supplied decomposition can eliminate them.

misconceptions.claim: One un-lowerable op forces the whole function into eager mode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only the specific op falls back; surrounding compilation continues.

misconceptions.claim: Inductor translates CUDA source to Triton at trace time.
Inductor inlines PTX of the fallback op into a single Triton kernel.
Fallbacks and graph breaks are the same thing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Graph breaks split the Dynamo trace; fallbacks are Inductor codegen boundaries.

implementationFacts: Fallback ops appear as ATen kernel calls in the generated wrapper code
Fusion boundaries at fallbacks add memory traffic for the fallback op's inputs/outputs
Users can register decompositions to reduce fallback frequency
performanceScenarios: A single fallback in a hot chain can cost significant HBM traffic; identifying it via inductor logs is a common optimization step.
